bindings.label: Patient developed erythema and edematous necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears three days after admission

Patient is a man in his 40s with a medical history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia who presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure; following admission, he was intubated with prone positioning and treatment was initiated
He was found to have Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia
Three days after admission, the patient developed erythema and edematous necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears; no devices had been used on the ears

The necrosis progressed during the following days, primarily involving the earlobe of the right ear and a large portion of the helix of the left ear; physical exam showed a 2 cm erythematous plaque with overlying eschar on the right earlobe and multiple erythematous edematous erosions with eschar and crust on the helical rim of the left ear
Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal and dermal necrosis with adnexal necrosis and sparse inflammation
Biopsy lacks vascular thrombi/hemorrhage and septic vasculitis
